fact: Clues are short and hooked, mostly mundane observations that turn ominous in hindsight, leave the last step to the reader, and live in journal, item lore, chronicle, beats or chatter.

Q1 (why do I remember nothing, answered B30-B31) is clued by the wrist mark, notes in the player's hand, the too-regular warm stone, the ledger-hound, the ward opening to a seal and to a charcoal copy once, keepers filing the player, N6's glance, and N8 reading the seal at B33.
source: mysteries.md#Question 1: why do I remember nothing? (answered at B30, B31)

fact: Q2 (have I been here before, answered B36) is clued by knowing which cellar to dig, the cellar stool and tally-board, the staring stranger and the re-tied snares, tallymen counting the old town's higher number, the marked camp on the map, N9 tying the knot back, and decades-old snares set the player's way.
source: mysteries.md#Question 2: have I been here before? (answered at B36)

fact: Q3 (why did the world break, answered B42) is clued by warm on purpose, ledger fragments in wasp nests, the Warm's songs of hearths going out one after another, N3's binding declines, the keel name N3 copies at B33, the B39 costing, and the registry's selection field.
source: mysteries.md#Question 3: why did the world break? (answered at B42)

fact: Q4 (what is under the land) is never answered; it is clued by the cooling, the breathing, the taboo never thank the warmth and the even draw at B47 with its journal figures; its journal entry has a header and three crossed-out false starts and never a fourth, and a Chequer note has respiration crossed out for cycle.
source: mysteries.md#Question 4: what is under the land? (never answered)

fact: Q5 (what did the previous me want, answered B49) is clued by torn stubs (B1), the cellar tally-board (B12), the re-tied snares (B16), the tally by the keel chamber cot (B30), a stool in every ruin layer (B36), the tick in the registry (B40), old cairns on the lamp road (B45), then the pages; the circles diagram shows only at day one's read by the fire (l_read), B24 and B49.
source: mysteries.md#Question 5: what did the previous me want? (answered at B49)

fact: Unanswered on purpose: what the Deep Account is, what the even draw was, where spent memory goes, whether the reserve covers the next Black Drift, the Leaners, the dune thing, why the stool's leg is always short, why N3 said no, what lies past the glow and whether other keels hold elsewhere.
The Chequer map shows several keel marks not crossed out, an expansion hook.

At most one ominous line per journal page; crossed-out guesses get corrected as the player learns; rare old-ink notes (old_hand_rate) are already present, come from the selves of towns 2 to 4, may contradict each other and are not always right; the later pages carry a few small pencil notes near the gutter.

The journal is the player's own; its front pages were torn out by the self of town 4, margin notes from towns 2 to 4 are in the player's hand, and a few later pages carry small pencil notes near the gutter, found as entries reach them.
The tone sample 'My gran said it used to be warm on purpose.' is a fireside clue available after B13.
source: mysteries.md#Question 3: why did the world break? (answered at B42)
